title: Check candidate roots of a converted log equation against the domain of the logarithms
content: When you eliminate logarithms to form a polynomial equation (e.g. by using 2 log(4-x) = log((4-x)^2) and then equating arguments), the resulting polynomial can have roots that are not actually solutions of the original equation. This happens if substituting a root back into the original expression makes the argument of any log negative or zero, since logs of non-positive numbers are undefined. After solving the polynomial, always substitute each candidate root back into every original log term and reject any root that produces a non-positive argument — state explicitly which log becomes undefined and why (e.g. 'x = 8 is rejected because log(4-8) = log(-4), which cannot be evaluated').
